terra.problem: The explanation adds a reason Ezekiel is told to wail. Marking it as a guess does not permit an unstated reason.
The pillow joke makes light of a message about doom for the nations.
The verse does not say news travels from Egypt or that it hurts people along the way.
The party and party-hat jokes make light of the slain and the anguish described in the verse.
The text does not say what everybody in Cush does.
The verse does not say Egypt’s allies fall first and her strength collapses afterward.
The verse says they will know He is the LORD; it does not state that God wants them to know as His reason for acting.
The verse does not say the messengers carry a warning or that the ships carry no cargo.
It says the baker has the “wrong direction,” using “wrong” about the answer.
The following verse mentions a prince, not princes.
The verse says God will instill fear; it does not say fear is the opposite of hope.
The verse says the arm was not bound or splinted. It does not say whether anyone set it.
A sword is held in the hand, not in the arm.
Calling the baker’s answer a “funny guess” makes the answer itself the joke.
The verse says the arm had not been splinted, not that it could not be splinted.
Verse 24 does not end the passage; verses 25 and 26 follow it.
